blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The scaling relationship of compute and performance for language models (LMs) has been extensively studied; more recently, models are being designed to scale memory use, as well. In particular, adding embeddings for n-grams scales memory separately from compute use, because each pass only processes individual embedding rows, which are much smaller than the storage used for the whole embedding table. However, existing methods train embeddings from scratch, which needs expensive GPU memory for fast reading and writing. Meanwhile, the ordinary memory of the host system is cheap and underutilized by these training methods. To scale on host memory, we introduce COUNT (Counting Offline Unlocks N-gram Transformers), which builds n-gram embeddings without adding learned parameters by storing precomputed n-gram counts on host. We use the corpus frequencies to weight together the LM's own unembeddings of the next tokens most often following the current n-gram history. At a fixed compute budget, COUNT can be added as an additional input embedding for pretraining 1B-parameter LMs to improve validation loss as much as an LM with 57% more compute. If GPU memory is limited, using COUNT to let backbone parameters fill GPU memory gives better performance than splitting memory with additional learned n-gram embeddings. Beyond efficiency, COUNT allows switching in a different table of n-gram counts from a domain-specific corpus at inference time to adapt to a new task without any training.
blocks.zh: 对语言模型(LM)的计算和性能的缩放关系进行了广泛的研究;最近还在设计模型,以扩大内存的使用。 特别是,为n-grams刻度内存添加嵌入与计算使用分开,因为每个通过只处理单个嵌入行,这比整个嵌入表所用的存储要小得多. 然而,现有的方法从零开始训练嵌入,这需要昂贵的GPU内存来进行快速读写. 同时,主机系统的普通记忆成本低廉,被这些训练方法利用不足. 要在主机内存上缩放,我们引入了COUNT(Counting Outline Unlocks N-gram Transformers),它通过存储主机上的预计算n-gm计数来构建n-gm嵌入,而不添加学到的参数. 我们用血清频率来测量 LM本身的未嵌入物 最常见的是随着当前的n-gm历史。 在固定的计算预算中,可添加COUNT,作为预先训练1B参数LMs的额外输入嵌入,以改善验证损失,其LM比计算多57%. 如果GPU内存是有限的,使用COUNT让骨干参数填充GPU内存比用额外的已学到的n-gm嵌入来拆分内存能产生更好的性能. 除了效率之外,COUNT允许在推论时间从一个特定域的目录中切换到一个不同的n-g计数表,以适应新的任务而无需经过任何训练.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Compute and memory are both crucial resources for scaling language models (LMs). The tradeoff of compute and performance has been improved through optimal allocation of compute to parameters and training tokens ( Kaplan et al., 2020 ; Hoffmann et al., 2022 ) . Beyond compute, performance can also be bought by increased memory through architectures that scale sparsely activated parameters, such as by activating only a subset of experts in mixture-of-experts (MoE) models ( Shazeer et al., 2017 ; Lepikhin et al., 2020 ; Fedus et al., 2022 ) .
The scaling of another type of sparsely activated parameters, input embeddings, has recently seen much exploration ( Roy et al., 2022 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Cheng et al., 2026 ) . By embedding n-grams as well as individual tokens, many new parameters can be added to the embedding table while each lookup still processes only one row. Thus, compute scales only with the width of the embedding not the much larger total size of the embedding table.
blocks.zh:
计算和内存既是衡量语言模型(LM)的关键资源. 计算与性能的取舍通过最佳分配计算参数和培训符号得到了改进(Kaplan等人,2020年;Hoffmann等人,2022年)。 除了计算之外,还可以通过放大稀有活性参数的架构来增加内存来购买性能,例如只激活一批专家混合模型(Shazeer等,2017;Lepikhin等,2020;Fedus等,2022)。
另一类稀有活性参数即输入嵌入物的缩放,最近经历了大量的探索(Roy等,2022;Huang等,2025;Liu等,2026;Cheng等,2026.). 通过嵌入正克以及单个符号,可以将许多新的参数添加到嵌入表上,而每个查询仍然只处理一行. 因此,只用嵌入的宽度来计算比例,而不是用嵌入表的总大小来计算。

blocks.en:
Existing n-gram embedding work learns representations from scratch jointly with pretraining. Consequently, they are not easily offloaded from expensive GPU memory during training, because their weights and optimizer state must be read and written quickly, increasing communication complexity.
Therefore these learned n-gram embeddings compete for GPU memory with the backbone model’s parameters.
But a long line of language modeling research and settled knowledge has built representations of n-grams without expensive pretraining by instead counting the frequency of n-grams in a corpus ( Jelinek and Mercer, 1980 ; Kneser and Ney, 1995 ; Brants et al., 2007 ) .
These methods refine the basic principle that the likelihood of a continuation can be estimated from counts of its occurrence after an n-gram history that is a suffix of the current context.
Existing work integrates such count-based language modeling or related corpus-retrieval methods with neural LMs ( Khandelwal et al., 2020 ; Li et al., 2022 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) . But unlike scaling dense input representations, these fuse raw next-token distributions at the output.
blocks.zh:
现有的正克嵌入工作与预训一起从零开始学习表示. 因此,在训练期间,它们不容易从昂贵的GPU内存中卸下,因为它们的重量和优化状态必须迅速被读取并写出,从而增加了通信的复杂性.
因此,这些已学习到的正克嵌入与主干模型的参数竞争GPU内存.
但是,一长串语言模型研究和定居知识通过计算一项文书中的正克频率(Jelinek和Mercer,1980年;Kneser和Ney,1995年;Brants等人,2007年),在不昂贵的预训的情况下建立了正克表达方式。
这些方法完善了以下基本原则:在n克历史作为当前上下文后缀之后,可以从其发生的计数中估算续作的可能性.
现有工作将这种基于计数的语言模型或相关实体检索方法与神经LM(Khandelwal等,2020年;Li等,2022年;Liu等,2025年b)结合起来。 但与缩放密集的输入表示不同,这些引信在输出时原始的相接式分布.

blocks.en:
We propose COUNT , Counting Offline Unlocks N-gram Transformers, which builds n-gram embeddings with precomputed corpus next-token statistics stored in host RAM.
COUNT connects the expressivity of learned embeddings with the read-only storage of count-based scores.
For each n-gram history, corpus counts supply a fixed list of frequent next tokens.
The backbone LM’s unembedding head already learns representations of these predicted next tokens, so COUNT uses frequency scores to weight and combine unembeddings of next tokens as a new input embedding summed with the token embedding.
This adds no learned parameters, and since the large counts table is read-only, it does not need to use GPU memory. Since COUNT’s count tables are computed offline, they can also be cheaply recomputed over new corpora to change its embeddings at inference time with no additional parameter training.

blocks.en: We train COUNT on a range of backbone LMs from 60M--1B parameters and token to parameter ratios from 10 to 40, allowing us to observe how COUNT interacts with traditional parameter and token scaling. We find that standard transformers without COUNT would need 46--89% more compute to achieve the same language modeling loss as COUNT and 6--56% more compute to match downstream task loss. Moreover, COUNT achieves Pareto-optimal tradeoffs between loss and learned parameter count in comparisons with learned n-gram embeddings, which need more GPU RAM to increase performance comparably. COUNT also improves performance more than output-level fusion of corpus counts. We also experiment with swapping in target-domain n-gram statistics at inference time and get training-free improvements in domain-specific evaluations in math, biomedicine, and law. We release 1 1 1 https://github.com/IanMagnusson/COUNT n-gram counts of the full Dolma 3 pretraining corpus ( Olmo et al., 2026 ) , along with training code and pretrained checkpoints for COUNT and learned n-gram baselines.

In our experiments we use stupid backoff ( Brants et al., 2007 ) to score observed continuations by their count ratio and otherwise back off to a shorter history with a discount. All of this can be done offline, before pretraining, at a fraction of the cost of training a large LM on the same corpus.

blocks.en: 3.2 Building n-gram tables
blocks.zh: 3.2 建造正克表格

blocks.en:
We count n-grams through order six over the full Dolma 3 ( Olmo et al., 2026 ) pretraining corpus and construct continuation scores using the stupid-backoff procedure in Section 2.3 .
To vary table size, we select which n-gram orders to store, prune low-count n-grams, discard histories below a history-count threshold, retain the top- K K continuations, and quantize their scores. Since host RAM is inexpensive, our flagship experiments use the largest n-gram table which is sized to saturate the host RAM available on our compute nodes. That 797 GB table serves the 370M, 600M, 760M, and 1B backbones; the 60M, 100M, and 190M backbones use a 17.1 GB table built by the same procedure with tighter count thresholds, so COUNT’s table capacity grows with backbone size across the ladder. See Appendix A.2 for all configurations of our primary table.

blocks.en:
Figure 3 compares standard transformers, COUNT, and learned n-gram embeddings with 60M–1B backbones by total learned parameters. Learned parameters are the primary driver of additional GPU memory footprint, so this comparison allows hardware-agnostic assessment of optimality with respect to memory. The Pareto frontier mostly follows COUNT, because its improvements add no learned parameters. Even where learned n-gram embeddings produce comparable performance, they do so at the cost of additional learned parameters to store learned n-gram embeddings, which cannot be easily offloaded during training and contend with backbone model parameters for GPU memory.
Each column fixes D / N D/N , so training tokens scale with the backbone rather than with added embedding parameters.
The Pareto frontier connects configurations with the lowest measured loss, or highest accuracy, for their parameter budget.

Unlike tables of n-gram embeddings learned from scratch, COUNT tables store scores over a shared vocabulary of next tokens; COUNT maps these scores into embeddings using the same unembedding basis. This allows the n-gram table to be modified at inference time without any training. We test two use cases where table swapping is desirable: whether a pretrained COUNT model can adapt to a new domain-specific table or a smaller table for a tight deployed host-memory budget.
Both experiments use COUNT pretrained on a 1B backbone at token-to-parameter ratios D / N ∈ { 10 , 20 , 40 } D/N\in\{10,20,40\} .

blocks.en:
The amount of host RAM at training time may be greater than what is available at deployment, so we ask how performance will degrade if we use a smaller n-gram count table at inference time. We replace the same model’s original table with general-domain tables of 459.222, 142.037, 68.458, and 17.114 GB at each training budget.
These tables vary in history-count and n-gram-count thresholds.
Figure 5 shows how much table storage can be removed while retaining better performance than a standard transformer.
On the 1B backbone COUNT checkpoints we can reduce storage by more than an order of magnitude while still improving on the standard transformer. Notably, this can be done at inference time without any training, as the larger and smaller tables all represent n-gram histories in the same format as next-token scores.

blocks.en: 6 Training and inference throughput

blocks.en:
While COUNT adds no learned parameters and can hide the host-resident table lookup time behind backbone LM GPU compute, we still need to measure its costs in practice.
Adding no learned parameters means no added cost in the C = 6 ​ N ​ D C=6ND sense and in parameter memory, but gathering selected unembedding rows is real work that the estimate omits and GPU footprint depends on more than parameters, so we measure throughput (Figure 6 ) and peak GPU memory (Table 10 ) directly.
These experiments use the 1B backbone parameter checkpoints of COUNT, learned n-gram embeddings, and standard transformer.
We measure training throughput as median tokens per second (TPS) of optimization steps 50-100 on 8 H200 GPUs.
For inference we measure prefill and decode on one H200 after warm-up batches. Appendix A.4 gives the measurement configurations and Appendix B.2 reports additional measured settings.

添加没有学到的参数意味着在C=6 N D C=6ND感和参数内存中没有增加成本,但是收集选定的未嵌入行是真正的工作,估计省略和GPU脚印取决于超过参数,因此我们直接测量吞吐量(图6)和高峰GPU内存(表10).

blocks.en:
COUNT has a small impact on throughput at the 1B backbone scale, retaining 93.1–97.8% of standard transformer training throughput, 95.5–95.8% for prompt prefill, and 95.9–96.7% for autoregressive decoding.
We use three optimizations to recover most of the standard transformer’s throughput: (1) compiled, multithreaded host lookup; (2) prefetching lookups for training and prefill tokens while the GPU processes the preceding batch; and (3) a fused embedding reduction that gathers and sums candidate vectors without storing them separately.

blocks.en:
We also optimize the learned n-gram embedding baseline that we compare against: (1) we implement sparse optimizer updates for only the retrieved embedding rows, avoiding a full-table gradient update at each step.
At 190M with a 17.1 GB learned n-gram table, full-table optimizer updates ran at 4.4% of standard transformer training throughput and updates to retrieved rows only at 96.3%, and the 1B learned baseline in Table 7 trains at 98.3%.
(2) We implement inference-time host offloading to gather learned embedding rows on the CPU and transfer them to the GPU, retaining 95.9–96.0% of standard transformer prefill throughput and 93.9–96.0% of decode throughput, similar to COUNT.

blocks.en: 7 Related work
blocks.zh: 7 相关工作

blocks.en: 7.1 N-grams in neural language models
blocks.zh: 7.1 神经语言模型中的N克

blocks.en:
There has been much work on learning embeddings for n-grams, especially in the past two years, with the motivation that scaling embeddings increases performance predictably ( Tao et al., 2024 ) .
The core problem all such work grapples with is that independently representing all | 𝒱 | n |\mathcal{V}|^{n} possible n-grams is quickly intractable.
One line of work uses multiple hashes of the n-grams to allow collisions that partially cancel out over different hash functions ( Roy et al., 2022 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) .
Other work builds embeddings of an n-gram based on learned representations of the tokens that it shares with lower n-gram orders ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) or combines token embeddings that make up the current n-gram suffix at inference time without any training ( Qu et al., 2026 ) .
Yet another approach is to use an auxiliary model to embed the n-grams ( Yu et al., 2025 ) .
Similarly, the backbone model’s own hidden state can provide the contextual information, and additional embeddings are keyed just by the current unigram but further conditioned by the hidden state ( Ding et al., 2026 ; Tseng and De Sa, 2026 ) .
This approach can also be used with hashed n-gram embeddings by having the hidden state of the model gate the inclusion of the embeddings ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
Most similar to our work, Neubig and Dyer (2016) actually mix count-based next-token distributions with neural predictions conditioned on some count-based n-gram features.
There is also more recent late-fusion-only work that interpolates the neural LM’s output distribution with a nonparametric one at inference time, from nearest neighbors over a datastore of contexts ( Khandelwal et al., 2020 ) or from unbounded-order Infini-gram counts ( Liu et al., 2025b ) . Li et al. (2022) instead train a neural LM with scaled n-gram log probabilities added to its output logits, yielding a multiplicative combination of the two distributions.
This work on late fusion of next-token frequencies also demonstrates domain adaptation at inference time ( Khandelwal et al., 2020 ; Li et al., 2022 ) .
In contrast to these approaches, our method can be seen as an early fusion combination of count-based and neural LMs where the count-based next-token distribution is represented directly in the shared embedding space of the neural LM.
We compare late fusion to COUNT in Appendix B.1 and find that late fusion does not benefit from inclusion in pretraining and does not improve generalist performance as much as COUNT.

最类似于我们的工作,"Neubig"和"Dyer"(2016年)实际上混合了基于计数的下位子分布与神经预测以一些基于计数的正克特征为条件.
也有一些较近期的后聚变唯能工作将神经LM的输出分布以非参数推论时间来插入,来自环境数据库的近邻(Khandelwal等人,2020年)或来自无限制的Infini-gram计数(Liu等人,2025年b). 李等编. (2022年)取而代之的是训练一个神经LM,其输出对数中增加了缩放的正克日志概率,产生了两个分布的多相组合.
这一关于晚聚下位频率的工作也表明在推论时间对域的适应(Khandelwal等人,2020年;Li等人,2022年)。
与这些方法相反,我们的方法可以看作是基于计数和神经LM的早期聚变结合,其中基于计数的下位子分布直接体现在神经LM的共享嵌入空间中.
我们在附录B.1中将后聚变与COUNT相提并论,发现后聚变不能从纳入预训中受益并不如COUNT那样能提高通论性能.

blocks.en:
Outside of academic literature, nanoGPT speed-run submissions concurrent with COUNT ( PR #367 and PR #380 ) and unpublished experiments discussed in a blog post by Infini-gram author Jiacheng Liu retrieve a sample of matching suffixes from training data and use their continuations to build a next-token hint from the token embeddings, which is then input to the LM backbone. Where these methods predict continuations from less than a hundred samples retrieved online, COUNT computes corpus frequencies over all occurrences in a full pretraining corpus offline. We compare also the use of the input token embedding or unembedding matrix as next-token basis in Appendix B.7 and find that our use of the unembedding performs best.
These engineering experiments highlight further opportunities for throughput optimization of count-based embeddings, complementing our systematic analysis across 60M–1B backbone scales, training budgets, and 74 downstream task evaluations.

blocks.en: 7.2 Tokenization and n-grams
blocks.zh: 7.2 肯化和正克

blocks.en:
A highly related thread of work explores n-gram tokens for a different motivation.
They address the arbitrariness of token segmentation by either exploring ways to segment further and then represent combinations of tokens ( Clark et al., 2022 ; Pagnoni et al., 2025 ) or by relaxing segmentation and allowing n-grams composed of many words to become single LM tokens ( Liu et al., 2025a ) .
blocks.zh:
一个高度相干的工作线索为不同的动机探索了n-gm符号.
他们通过探索进一步分出的方式,然后代表了分出物的组合(Clark等,2022;Pagnoni等,2025),或者通过放松分出并允许由多词组成的正克成为单LM分出物(Liu等,2025a.),来解决分出物的任意性.

blocks.en: 7.3 Retrieval-augmented language models
blocks.zh: 7.3 检索语言模型

blocks.en:
Though architecturally unrelated, retrieval-augmented LMs ( Guu et al., 2020 ; Lewis et al., 2021 ; Borgeaud et al., 2022 ; Asai et al., 2023 ; Shao et al., 2024 ) share a motivation with COUNT: access to nonparametric information from a raw corpus can complement the parametric knowledge learned by the LM when it trains on the same data.
Notably, retrieval also provides the affordance of zero-training domain adaptation.
Where these methods practically differ from COUNT is that their nonparametric information is input directly as a token sequence into the LM, increasing context usage and compute.
Also because COUNT stores only counts, its data store will always be much smaller than storing the raw corpus it is fit on.
blocks.zh:
虽然在建筑学上无关紧要,但检索-增强的LMs(Guu等,2020年;Lewis等,2021年;Borgeaud等,2022年;Asai等,2023年;Shao等,2024年)与COUNT有着共同的动机:从生体获取非参数化信息可以补充LM在同一数据上训练时学到的参数化知识.
值得注意的是,检索还提供了零培训领域的适应。
如果这些方法实际上与COUNT不同,则其非参数信息直接作为符号序列输入LM,增加上下文使用和计算。
此外,由于COUNT只存储数,它的数据储存将永远比储存它适合的原始体小得多。

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
High-bandwidth GPU memory is the scarcest and most expensive resource in current training and serving hardware, while host RAM is cheaper per byte and largely uncontended by the model itself.
Learned n-gram embeddings buy their gains with parameters and optimizer state that must sit in GPU memory alongside the backbone.
COUNT buys comparable gains with bytes on cheaper memory, leaving GPU memory for backbone parameters.
Representing n-grams by counts also opens possibilities beyond efficiency.
A table of counts is an aggregate statistic rather than a corpus, so sharing it is often less sensitive and more compact than sharing the documents it summarizes, which offers a new way to ingest data that cannot be released as text.
N-gram frequencies can also be estimated from far less data than pretraining requires.
With only a small amount of domain-specific data we fit count-based priors that steered a generalist, pretrained model to better in-domain performance.
The long history of settled knowledge on count-based language modeling can likely produce useful next-token priors on even smaller corpora that are too small for parametric learning.
Finally, because each row lists the next-token candidates and scores for a history, the prior a COUNT model consults can be read, corrected, or extended directly, by editing rows rather than by retraining.

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: This work aims to make language models more efficient in order to lower the cost and environmental impact of building and running them. By moving n-gram memory from GPU memory to host RAM and adding no learned parameters, COUNT lets smaller models reach quality that would otherwise require more compute or more expensive hardware, and its tables can be built from modest corpora. We hope this helps a wider range of people and organizations, including those with limited compute or limited data, to train and use capable models. COUNT also changes what a data contributor has to share: an n-gram count table records how often continuations follow short contexts, not the documents themselves, and is therefore less sensitive than raw pretraining text, although high-order counts over rare contexts can still reveal fragments of the source and should be released with the same care as other derived statistics. Our experiments use publicly available pretraining data and evaluation suites.

blocks.en: A.4 Throughput configurations
blocks.zh: A.4 吞吐量配置

blocks.en:
All throughput measurements use the 1B ladder configuration, include lookup and host–GPU transfer in the timed workload, use the 1:1 input-embedding-to-backbone parameter ratio for the learned n-gram baseline, keep COUNT tables in host RAM, and (for inference) use D / N = 40 D/N=40 checkpoints on C4 validation prompts.
Compiled lookup searches sorted histories with multiple CPU threads; lookup caching reuses retrieved results; prefetch prepares lookups while the GPU processes the preceding batch; fused embedding combines row gathering and weighted summation; sparse updates optimize only retrieved learned n-gram rows; host offloading keeps learned n-gram tables on the CPU with their projections on the GPU; KV caching and CUDA graphs are the usual inference optimizations.
Tables 4 – 6 give the settings for each workload.
